episode.title: Different Ways of Thinking
intro: Mika joins a team meeting in Tokyo. They talk about a new travel campaign. People have different ideas, so they must talk politely.
ミカは東京でチーム会議に参加します。新しい旅行キャンペーンについて話します。意見が違うので、ていねいに話す必要があります。
goal: I can read different opinions and explain an idea with a simple reason.
異なる意見を読み、簡単な理由を付けて案を説明できる。
episode.warmup: When you disagree at work, what do you say first?
words: I think this idea can work.
この案はうまくいくと思います。
この客層はより多くの収入につながります。
両方の層を比べましょう。
We need the same hotel style.
同じホテルのスタイルが必要です。
もっと情報が必要です。
discussion: Why was Mika’s idea helpful in the meeting?
なぜミカのアイデアは会議で役に立ちましたか？
episode.followup: In your job or school, what data do you want to see before you decide?

rule: Use I think ... because ... to give an opinion and a reason.
I think ... because ... で意見と理由を伝えましょう。
examples: I think this photo is good because it shows the rooms.
部屋が写っているので、この写真がよいと思います。

rule: Read each person's idea. Use I see your point, but ... to add another idea.
それぞれの案を読みましょう。I see your point, but ... で別の案を加えられます。
examples: I see your point, but we can compare both groups.
お考えは分かりますが、両方の層を比べられます。

situation: You and your tutor talk about the meeting story and check understanding.
講師と会議のストーリーについて話し、内容を確認します。
apply.text:
Ethan: Younger travellers use social media. We can reach them there. Some may return for future trips.

Daichi: The client's research says business guests bring more income. We should not forget them.

Mika: Could we make one message for each group?

Soo-jin: That may work. Both messages need the same hotel style. Let's check the information before choosing.

After the meeting, Ethan tells Mika she did well. The team has not chosen a final plan.
questions: Why does Daichi focus on business guests?
They bring more income in the client's research.

choose: I (think / thinking) the photo is good.
It is clear (because / before) it shows the rooms.
Both messages (need / needs) the same style.
choices: What does Daichi use to support his idea?
The same hotel style in both messages.

situation: You are Mika from Osaka, a new team member at Eastbridge in Tokyo.
あなたは大阪出身で、東京のイーストブリッジに入ったばかりのミカです。
task: Say what can stay and what needs changing. Give one reason and ask a question.
変えなくてよい点と直す点を伝えましょう。理由を一つ話し、質問を一つしましょう。
mission.text:
Review note

Both messages use the same hotel colours. Keep them.

The younger-traveller message has a clear photo. The business-traveller message needs a shorter headline.

Mika, please shorten that headline. Ethan will check costs. Daichi will check the research.

Bring the updates to Soo-jin at three. Do not publish the ads yet.
mission.title: Review note
lines: Mika, what can we keep in both messages?
Why can a short headline help?
Who will check costs and research?
mission.evidence: Keep the hotel colours. Shorten the business headline. Ethan checks costs, Daichi checks research, and updates go to Soo-jin at three. No publication yet. Accept a short reason, such as easier to read.

topics: Do you like to speak first in meetings?
What helps you explain your opinion clearly?
How do you show respect when you disagree?
Who spends more money, in your experience?
Do you prefer younger or older customers for a product?
What is one good way to reach customers?
What data is important in your job or school?
When do you decide without data?
How do you check if data is reliable?
trivia: Many marketing teams use A/B testing to compare two message ideas.
多くのマーケティングチームはA/Bテストで2つのメッセージ案を比較します。
triviaQuestion: Two versions, like message A and message B.
episode.closing: The team did not decide yet. Daichi wants to check the data, and Ethan tells Mika she did well.

review.manualReview: Reviewed and edited for the new friendship-only outline, simple language, explicit roles, fresh reading evidence and consistent keys.
